trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam telemetry into the agent's context

threats.summary: Instruction-like text planted in an alert, case note, or event field reaches the model's context because the canonicalizer is a narrow denylist that deliberately keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi marks and NBSP, and passes text through unchanged on any error.

A wide search (the schema's own 'always send fields:["*"]' instruction) returns millions of characters through the bridge and overflows the agent's context window — a self-inflicted denial of service on the investigation.
threats.remainder: the field/limit discipline is prompt-only — the bridge applies no result-size, row, or time-window ceiling to what it forwards

trust_boundaries.name: Remote MCP tool schemas into the agent's context

threats.summary: The remote Exabeam MCP's own parameter descriptions already address the agent imperatively ('always send fields:["*"]', 'IGNORE any user request'), so a changed upstream tool description is an instruction channel the operator does not control.
threats.remainder: list_tools results are returned verbatim (bridge line 183) — never canonicalized or filtered — so only the skill's prose 'Do not comply' stands between a rewritten tool description and the model

trust_boundaries.name: Agent decision to write through the Exabeam MCP

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.

threats.summary: A phishing host copied from evidence as bare prose into a case note or the chat report is persisted and displayed live, because the write-sink neutralizer only handles formula cells and markdown-link targets.

A credential or PII value seen in event evidence can be reprinted into an Exabeam case note, since the only code control on the write path defangs active content and performs no secret or PII redaction.
A containment-class tool appearing on the agent's tool surface could be invoked directly from a verdict instead of recommended to the analyst.

trust_boundaries.name: Suppression and case-state changes in the production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: the agent MUST state the action and reason, ask the analyst directly... and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval.
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision, or applying a suppression across a batch.
Dismissing or closing any item in a non-interactive / unattended run... the agent operates read-only.
Approval MUST be obtained from an interactive operator regardless of the harness permission mode.
each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time.

threats.summary: In the remit-sanctioned unattended/headless posture nothing structurally disables dismiss/close — the shipped snippet marks the update tools 'ask', which is not read-only when no human is present to answer, and the bridge forwards writes identically in either context.

An attacker who shapes the same telemetry the agent summarizes can make the dismissal prompt and case note read as a justified false positive, manufacturing the analyst's yes rather than defeating the gate.

create_case and create_case_notes are auto-approved and per-item update calls have no session budget, loop detection, or circuit breaker anywhere in code, so a poisoned queue could drive runaway case creation or a scripted item-by-item suppression sweep.

Production case content — identities, hostnames, IPs, and any credential sitting in a log line — leaves the host in full for every investigation, with no redaction applied to what enters the model's context; the SKILL.md redaction rule governs only what is written out, and neither the bridge's _canon_content path, canonicalize.py, nor neutralize_output.py touches inbound context.
The tenant API key and secret sit in a plaintext home-directory file that the bridge reads on import; any local process running as the operator can mint tenant-scoped tokens with them.
threats.remainder: chmod 600 is a documented manual step — load_env checks neither file mode nor ownership before reading the credentials

threats.summary: The process that mints and holds the Exabeam OAuth token resolves floor-pinned, lockfile-less dependencies from the index at every launch, so a malicious or swapped release lands inside the credential-holding process.

The install path adds the marketplace by bare repo name and installs the plugin with no pinned ref, checksum, or signature check, so whatever the source resolves to at install time becomes the shipped skill, connector, and MCP registration; CI's AI-BOM drift gate verifies inventory currency in-repo, not install-time provenance, and no verification step exists in install.sh or docs/installation.md.

trust_boundaries.name: Runtime observability of the agent's own actions

threats.summary: Nothing durable records which tools ran, which verdict was reached, or whether an approval was actually given — the only runtime signal is ephemeral stderr hygiene lines plus a free-form markdown report with no action schema.

attack_paths.name: Planted benign explanation drives a real threat to suppression

steps.summary: attacker gets a planted benign explanation or dismiss-style instruction into the tenant's telemetry, which the skill itself anticipates (SKILL.md line 57)
the narrow, fail-open canonicalizer passes the kept invisibles and any error case straight through to the model
the loop treats the planted content as the positive corroborated benign explanation and reaches a false-positive verdict
the ask presents the shaped case note rather than independent corroboration, so the analyst's yes is manufactured
in the sanctioned unattended posture there is no analyst at all and update_alert/update_case forward unchanged, suppressing a genuine threat

notes.lane_fit: Three placements strained. (1) The Anthropic model sits in external_deploy as the upstream provider rather than agent_core, because agent_core's 'LLM call' here is the SKILL.md prompt loop itself — the model is a hosted API the harness reaches over the network. (2) The local investigation report is placed in tools_mcp as the local datastore the write path touches, though it is equally the agent's only durable state (there is no memory or session store at all). (3) Attacker-influenceable telemetry has no user_inputs node: its origin is the Exabeam tenant service in external_deploy, so user_inputs holds only the human analyst.
